criterion_logic_audit.assessment: A manually confirmed complete source chain with gold R3=0 conflicts with the uploaded criterion's positive condition. Gold R3=1 without a recovered complete chain is unresolved rather than a logical contradiction because the extractor may have missed evidence and historical practice may use a weaker ROCKMAG-style proxy.

interpretation.gold_one_no_candidate: Frozen retrieval/extraction misses or possible criterion-practice mismatch; absence of a recovered candidate is not evidence that the paper lacks evidence.
interpretation.support_gold_zero: Empirical conflict candidates requiring manual confirmation of target binding and own-study scope; not automatically proven label errors.

University of Nairobi, PO Box 30197, Nairobi, Kenya Received 1978 December 1; in original form 1978 April 18 Summary. This paper reports a palaeomagnetic study of the lower Proterozoic granites, exposed in the western part of Kenya and dated at 2530 k 50 Ma (ARb = 1.39 x lO-"yr-'). Ten sites out of 13 have yielded stable palaeo- magnetic directions which are believed to be primary. Polished section and thermomagnetic analyses indicate titanomagnetite grains as the main carrier of the primary component of the natural remanence. The mean palaeo- magnetic north pole is calculated at 2 10.7" E, 60.9" N with Ag5 = 13.5".

Three axial plane traces were observed in the folds of these rocks and suggest three phases of deformation and metamorphic activity in them. Petrographic studies indicated the presence of orthopyroxene as a primary metamorphic mineral, and secondary development of garnet and amphibole around ferrohypersthene margins and in the crushed zones (Subba Rao 1974). These lead to the interpretation that both the original ferruginous quartzites and granites were deposited together, and were involved in the initial stage of tectonism and metamorphism probably at 2590 Myr giving rise to quartz-magnetites and explaining the presence of orthopyroxene. 3.2. Results One of the main objectives of this study is to reveal the characteristic magnetization in the red beds of the Chilgok Formation. Typical thermomagnetic results in this study suggest magnetite and hematite to be the predominant magnetic minerals in the samples. The unblocking temperatures of about 570° –575 °C and 675° –680 °C conﬁrm the presence of magnetite and hematite, respectively. The irreversible portion of the cooling cycle may result from the creation of new ferromagnetic minerals from the paramagnetic and superpara- magnetic materials due to recrystallization during heating (Fig. A1).

candidate_definitions.high_confidence_criterion: high-confidence proxy plus a named carrier and an explicit connection to remanence significance in the same source scope
candidate_definitions.high_confidence_proxy: exclusive target-bound same source scope with an own-study performed method and a carrier or diagnostic concept
candidate_definitions.medium_confidence: own-study method and companion evidence distributed across frozen target/sample/component-linked scopes
candidate_definitions.no_frozen_candidate: the frozen extractor recovered no qualifying candidate; this is not a scientific assertion that evidence is absent from the paper
